sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties network (e.g., BLEU–China BIT)
Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Convention (effective 1996, as amended by Protocol of 29 May 2009)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (23 August 2012, as amended)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Agreement (in force since 1 March 2019)
Luxembourg–Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement (17 June 1968, as amended)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (5 December 1967, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML Law, as amended); Loi modifiée du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE Law); Règlement grand-ducal du 26 mars 2019 relatif au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Loi modifiée du 5 avril 1993 relative au secteur financier (CSSF supervisory framework); Règlement CSSF n° 12-02 du 14 décembre 2012 sur la lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent et le financement du terrorisme (as amended); CSSF AML/CFT circulars and Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) supervisory practice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified true copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (acte notarié) or competent notary/consulate in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) for documents issued in non-Luxembourg jurisdictions; Luxembourg notarial certification for local execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence (attestation de résidence fiscale) of each corporate shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax administration of the shareholder's or UBO's jurisdiction of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatory jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent extract from the commercial register and certificate of incorporation of each corporate shareholder or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or commercial register of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatory jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of registered office / current address certificate of each corporate shareholder or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar, registered agent, or competent municipal authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatory jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming origin of funds and source of wealth of the contributing partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank or regulated financial institution providing the reference
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille with notarized signature; alternatively Consular Legalization where the bank so requires

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-notarization screening of all UBOs, partners, and the general partner against: (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list (CFSP); (iii) OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (US SDN); (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury (UK) consolidated list; and (v) Luxembourg national freezing measures and CRF red-flag indicators. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification applies on a risk-sensitive basis under FATF Recommendation 12, Article 3-2 of the AML Law, and CSSF Regulation 12-02; enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds documentation are required where any PEP, adverse media, or sanctions hit is identified. In accordance with CJEU Case C-37/20, RBE public access is restricted; due-diligence access remains available to obliged entities. Screening evidence must be archived for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); online availability search and e-filing via www.lbr.lu and the RCSL e-Justice portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings and the articles of association (statuts) must be drawn up in Luxembourgish, French, or German; an English-language original must be accompanied by a certified translation into one of those administrative languages. Only Latin-script characters are admitted in the registered name; non-Latin-script names of foreign parent companies must be transliterated consistently in the articles and registration filings. The registered name of a Société en Commandite Spéciale must close with the mandatory suffix 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Misleading financial-license tokens: 'Banque', 'Bank', 'Assurance', 'Réassurance', 'Fiduciaire', 'Trust', 'SICAV', 'FCP' used by an entity without the corresponding regulated license
Misleading legal-form tokens: 'SA', 'SARL', 'S.A.', 'société anonyme' used in the name of a partnership that is not incorporated under that form
State-patronage or sovereign-authority tokens: 'Luxembourg', 'État', 'Grand-Duché', 'Commune', 'État de Luxembourg', 'Chambre de Commerce' where implying official capacity or state sponsorship
Tokens requiring prior ministerial or sectoral approval before registration
Sector-descriptive tokens ('holding', 'participations', 'soparfi') that are materially inconsistent with the declared corporate object of the SPV
Words contrary to public order, good morals, or protected trademarks under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended) and LBR administrative practice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg law does not provide an extension for name clearance. A proposed name rejected by the RCS registrar may be re-submitted immediately in an amended form. Upon a formal, reasoned refusal, the applicant may: (i) request a written statement of reasons from LBR; (ii) file an administrative complaint with the Ministère de la Justice as supervisory authority; and (iii) seek judicial review before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre commerciale) within the statutory appeal period (generally one month of notification), represented by an avocat à la Cour. The negative-name certificate, when issued, is commonly treated as valid for 30 days, after which a fresh name-availability confirmation must be obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for RCS registration: the SCSp must have a fixed and physical registered office (siège social) in Luxembourg that is accessible to public authorities and at which statutory books and corporate documents are kept. Commercial domiciliation by a licensed domiciliation company under the Law of 31 May 1999 (Loi portant réglementation de la domiciliation de sociétés) is acceptable for a passive pure-equity holding SCSp, provided the provider maintains physical premises, mail-handling, and local compliance-contact capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated <5% annual probability) for a compliant, domiciled, pure-equity SCSp with timely RBE filings and no AML triggers; elevated to approximately 20-30% where the SCSp is registered at a mass-domiciliation address monitored by the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) or where the UBO profile results in enhanced scrutiny.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing fee (LBR registration dossier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and company register filing fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES) publication fee
Notarial deed of constitution (acte notarié) of the SCSp, coordination with RCS and legalization of annexes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary appointed within the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial emolument schedule of the Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg; market range EUR 1,200-2,000 depending on complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO initial declaration and RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the RBE register
Market benchmark for LBR name-search certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees: drafting of the limited partnership agreement (LPA), articles of association, partner resolutions, and compliance protocols
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; Luxembourg counsel hourly rates (EUR 250-450/hour) or fixed incorporation package
Market benchmark for physical registered office, mail handling and compliance-contact service (EUR 2,500-5,000/year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC file preparation: PEP, OFAC, UN/EU sanctions screening, and adverse-media checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per complete UBO screening package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of corporate documents of foreign shareholders and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Originating-state competent authority (foreign ministry/apostille office) and Luxembourg consular post where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official certification and consular fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account remote-opening facilitation and counterparty due-diligence package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fee may be waived or capitalized by the account bank

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (LSC), Articles 125-1 to 125-35 (Special Limited Partnership / SCSp) inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 February 2021 on RCS filing requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) and RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations); filings made electronically via eJustice.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution — the SCSp articles of limited partnership agreement executed before a Luxembourg notary, filed with the RCS and published in RESA; legal personality arises on the day of RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital, no paid-up capital threshold and no escrow or blocked-account requirement for an SCSp. The limited partner's contribution is freely fixed in the limited partnership agreement; capital may be contributed in cash, in kind or as services and remaining commitments are contractual.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner adopts the limited partnership agreement of the Luxembourg Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) as executed before the notary; RESOLVED, that the interests subscribed by the initial Limited Partner are accepted and the agreed capital contribution is recorded in the capital account; RESOLVED, that the SCSp's registered office be established at [address], Luxembourg, and that the representative appointed by the General Partner is vested with full authority before banks, tax authorities and the Luxembourg Business Registers; RESOLVED, that the opening of a bank account and the filing of the constitutive deed for RCS registration and RESA publication are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/KYC Due Diligence and Governance Definition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg professional formation agent (notary, law firm or registered fiduciary) acting under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector and CSSF AML/CTF rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect and verify the identity, residence and source of funds of every general and limited partner; identify all natural persons behind the SCSp for later RBE filing; define the governance rules (exclusive management by the general partner, reserved consent rights of the limited partner) and prepare the draft limited partnership agreement together with the pro-forma first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of all partners/UBOs
Proof of source of funds and source of wealth
Corporate registry extracts for corporate partners
Draft limited partnership agreement and governance matrix
Power of attorney in favour of the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any KYC request is raised, supplements must be filed within 10 calendar days; a Sanctions-list hit triggers enhanced due diligence and may require substitution of the affected partner before formation proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Check at RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run the proposed SCSp corporate name through the RCS online corporate-name database to verify there is no identical, confusingly similar or reserved name; confirm that the legal form suffix 'SCSp' appears in the name; no formal name reservation token exists in Luxembourg, so the chosen name is locked at filing time.
required_dossiers: Proposed name including 'SCSp' suffix
Copies of identity/KYC documents already gathered
Statement on the SCSp's sole corporate purpose (ISIC 6420 passive holding)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, file two alternative names in the same session; the RCS rejection note is administrative only and is cured by amending the proposed corporate name before notarisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Formation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) or private-deed signing in standard practice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All general and limited partners, or their attorneys-in-fact, appear before the notary for execution of the Acte de constitution; the notary verifies legal capacity, lawful purpose and consent, and delivers the authentic expédition required for RCS registration. A private deed is admissible only where the SCSp has no real-estate contribution and no gratuitous contribution.
required_dossiers: Final draft limited partnership agreement
Power of attorney where a partner appears by proxy
Passport copies and proof of address of each partner
Negative tax-debt certificate for any corporate partner
Consent of the registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries capacity or purpose, provide the corrected corporate authorisations or an updated deed; where notarisation cannot be completed, the parties may execute a private deed unless immovable or gratuitous contributions are present.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers via eJustice.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration form on eJustice.lu with the notarial expédition, registered office consent, list of authorised signatories and specimen signatures; pay the RCS filing fee (approximately EUR 78 / USD 85, updated by LBR from time to time); legal personality of the SCSp is acquired upon registration.
required_dossiers: RCS electronic registration form
Certified copy of the formation deed
Registered-office consent letter
List of managing representatives with specimen signatures
Filing power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS raises a query, respond within 15 calendar days by uploading the corrected data; a substantive amendment requires a rectifying rider certified by the notary and refiled through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) — Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, LBR automatically publishes the statutory data and the coordination of the deed in RESA; the publication reference should be verified and retained in the corporate file; publication is statutory and free of charge.
required_dossiers: RCS registration receipt
Certified coordination/clauses of the Acte de constitution
RCS number already assigned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a publication contains a material error, file a requête en rectification with RCS and republish the corrected deed in RESA; minor clerical errors are corrected directly by LBR upon written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) — Luxembourg Business Registers via eJustice.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RBE declaration within one month after RCS registration, identifying any natural person holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the SCSp's capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control; the declaration accompanies the proof of the ownership chain and is subject to civil and criminal penalties if omitted.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form with UBO identification
Ultimate beneficial ownership chart
Passport copies of the ultimate natural persons
RCS registration number of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RBE challenges the ownership chain, file an updated declaration with full documentary proof; prompt self-correction mitigates fines, which escalate per week of delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Rails Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institutions (representative of the Luxembourg Bankers' Association; no ministry window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the constitutional pack to the chosen Luxembourg bank and complete the AML/CTF onboarding, including UBO attestation and source-of-funds evidence; activate the Swift/Wire payment rails and execute the account mandate within the authority granted by the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and RESA publication copy
RBE filing acknowledgement
Notarial deed as filed
Board resolution appointing authorised signatories
KYC documents and source of funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, deliver audit-backed source-of-funds evidence or a clean UBO attestation; alternatively, a second Luxembourg bank or a local professional intermediary may complete onboarding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction générale des classes moyennes et PME (business establishment licensing directorate) — not applicable to a passive SCSp equity-holding vehicle
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment license) — not required for ISIC 6420 pure equity holding; the SCSp holds no operating establishment and exercises no regulated commercial or industrial activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category E: pure equity-holding SPV with no physical facility, no construction and no operational emission source; no EIA study or environmental registration required under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero discharge and zero emission operations; no wastewater, VOC or hazardous waste streams generated. If the SCSp later acquires serviced office premises, the hosting building must remain compliant with municipal wastewater discharge limits and EU air quality standards (Directive 2008/50/EC) as enforced by the Administration de l'environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — the SCSp has no physical plant and no employees. Where a registered office is hosted by a serviced-office provider, the landlord must maintain a valid fire-safety certificate, building occupancy permit and compliance with Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) requirements; no Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) workplace clearance is triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified e-Government portal: myguichet.lu / guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the business registration number (matricule), which functions as the tax identification number for the entity. 2) If the SCSp needs a VAT identification number, file a VAT registration application with the AEDT via myguichet.lu, after registration at the LBR. 3) Non-resident general partners and partners must obtain a Luxembourg personal tax matricule from the ACD through the local commune administration. 4) A foreign entity that is not established in Luxembourg but makes taxable supplies must appoint an approved Luxembourg VAT representative. 5) No minimum capital or physical office requirement is imposed for an SCSp, but substance evidence should be maintained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election. An SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; no domestic election exists to render it opaque. Affirmative elections are limited to VAT grouping (assujetti unique) and certain participation exemption holdings; hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD and EU Directive 2016/1164 operate mandatorily. A taxable entity-level regime would require conversion into a corporate vehicle such as a SOPARFI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the small business franchise exemption; mandatory VAT registration is required for taxable persons exceeding this threshold, and in any event for businesses supplying taxable goods or services where input VAT deduction is requested. Intra-Community distance sales to Luxembourg consumers become registrable above the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold unless an option is made.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or transaction-level API reporting exists for B2B invoices under Luxembourg VAT. E-invoicing is required only in the B2G segment, where invoices to Luxembourg public sector entities must be issued in a structured electronic format (PEPPOL) through the national procurement platform. Ordinary VAT invoices may be transmitted electronically subject to authenticity and integrity controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of movable goods dispatched or transported to a third country or territory qualifies for a 0% VAT rate provided the goods have left Luxembourg and the customs territory of the EU within 90 days of supply, the supplier retains documentary proof of dispatch/transport, and a valid Luxembourg customs export declaration has been lodged. Selected services relating to international trade (e.g., transport of goods to third countries, handling and storage incidental to export, and services directly linked to exports) may also be zero-rated. Intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered customers are zero-rated subject to valid VAT identification numbers and filing of a recapitulative statement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Luxembourg Customs electronic export declaration (e-DEU/DAU) and the customs movement reference number (MRN)
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, or airway bill evidencing physical export from the EU
Proof of export delivery or customs exit confirmation
Inward remittance certificate or bank payment evidence matching the invoiced amount
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow the 0% rate and reassess VAT at 17% when export documentation is missing, unreliable, or forged, or when the goods did not actually leave the EU within the prescribed time frame. Interest on late VAT, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, and penalties up to double the evaded VAT may apply for negligent or intentional offences. In cases of fraudulent export schemes, criminal prosecution, imprisonment, joint liability of directors and partners, and indefinite or extended statutory limitation periods apply. The exporter is also liable to repay any input VAT previously credited against the zero-rated supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the eurozone national central bank acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and the TARGET2 settlement framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) exercises banking licensing and AML/CFT supervision, while the BCL operates balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: EUR is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63-66 TFEU. No Luxembourg controls impede profit remittance, dividends, interest, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds from the SCSp to non-residents. The transparent SCSp itself suffers no withholding tax; only tax-resident partners may trigger standard withholding and CRS/FATCA reporting. No FX permit, quota, or central-bank pre-approval is applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender regime exists: Luxembourg imposes no timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation threshold for export receipts or any commercial proceeds. Multi-currency proceeds may be held indefinitely in resident or offshore accounts, converted freely at market rates, or re-deployed directly into target investments without BCL approval; this is immaterial to a passive ISIC 6420 holding SPV.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow and operational multi-currency (EUR/USD) accounts
Operational treasury account with dedicated EBH/KYC team and separate capital-contribution sub-accounts
Capital escrow account (compte séquestre) and operational multi-currency account
Operational holding-company account with integrated treasury and payment platform
EU cross-border operational account under standard partnership CDD
Operational account; capital escrow only with an existing group relationship

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for operational disbursements and LOW for capital escrow and treasury concentration. An EEA-authorised e-money institution or payment institution may passport into Luxembourg and supply multi-currency IBANs, SEPA, and wire rails without a Luxembourg credit-institution licence; however, an SCSp cannot legally rely on a non-EEA 'offshore digital EMI' because settling capital calls and safeguarding escrowed funds requires a CSSF-licensed credit institution under the Law of 22 May 2019 on payment services and the amended Law of 8 January 1993 on the financial sector. Such offshore EMIs are legally unavailable in Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default standard: the general partner's authorised signatories must attend an onboarding interview in Luxembourg or at the bank's group branch. Remote video verification is permitted only on a bank-discretionary, risk-based basis and only where all signatories hold verifiable EU eIDAS electronic identities and the partnership documents are apostilled/certified; fully remote opening without a prior relationship is systematically rejected by tier-1 banks. Where attendance is impractical, banks accept a notarised power of attorney with apostille, original certified corporate documents, and a live video identity confirmation, albeit with an enhanced-risk tag.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated pass-through SCSp with no CSSF licence and no minimum capital presuming an opaque unregulated fund or wealth-concealment vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed limited partnership agreement (LPA) evidencing a genuine commercial holding purpose; capital commitment schedule and drawdown ledger; general partner constitutional documents and Register of Commerce excerpt; RBE beneficial-owner filing confirmation; each limited partner's identity papers, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth letters, and CRS/FATCA self-certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tiered non-resident ownership exceeding three levels or ultimate owners in FATF-flagged / sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart through to natural persons; certified passports, residential proof, PEP/sanctions screening results; audited group financials; negative-news due-diligence report; written commercial rationale for the Luxembourg SPV; and confirmation that all partnership interests are registered or certificated for traceability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No Luxembourg substance (domiciliation agent only; management decisions taken abroad) creating a letter-box entity red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance binder: authorised domiciliation agreement, GP board minutes and decision logs, bank-mandate approvals, IT/communications proof, employment or service contracts of Luxembourg personnel, and an ATAD/CRS-relevant governance matrix demonstrating Luxembourg management substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity contributions from a non-bank related party with weak provenance, potentially re-characterised as loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notice and dated exhibit; notarised contribution and acquisition agreements for target equity; contributor's audited balance sheet and pre-funding bank statements; complete funding-chain memorandum from the remitting bank; and a Luxembourg tax legal opinion classifying the inflow as equity capital and rejecting thin-capitalisation treatment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EUR injections settle same-day in central-bank money over TARGET2 via the Luxembourg beneficiary bank, instructed by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer. Instructions must carry the Luxembourg BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for intra-group equity capital and must reference the capital-call notice; the receiving bank applies EU/UN (and US OFAC where relevant) sanctions screening, verifies remitter and UBO documentation, source-of-funds evidence, and the funding chain, and books the credit to the partnership's capital ledger under the LPA. Non-EUR tranches (USD, GBP, CHF) clear through SWIFT MT103 with MT202 COV cover via CHIPS/Fedwire, CHAPS, or SIC correspondents and convert at the bank's spot fixing; no Luxembourg FX declaration is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The passive equity SPV ordinarily issues no trade disbursements; downstream funding to target operating companies is cleared via SWIFT MT103 over TARGET2/SEPA for EUR, and MT202 COV through US/UK/Swiss correspondent rails for foreign currency. Where documentary credit is used for underlying acquisitions or target trade flows, the rail is a commercial letter of credit issued by SWIFT MT700, amended by MT707, negotiated under MT752, and reimbursed by MT103/MT202 COV, all under UCP 600. Every outgoing instruction carries the correct BOP purpose code and intra-group reference to preserve the pass-through equity accounting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR cross-currency spot and outright forwards with Luxembourg or EU credit institutions under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market or restricted currencies of underlying target jurisdictions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) hedging target-currency equity exposures against the EUR funding base
Purchased European-style FX call and put options for staged acquisition commitments
Multi-currency cash-pooling and auto-sweep arrangements that minimise spot FX conversion within the bank treasury desk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered particulars (confirmation annuelle RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of each calendar year; first confirmation due in the calendar year following initial registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file after a formal reminder triggers an administrative late fee and, after repeated non-compliance, administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS under Article 20 of the Law of 19 December 2002.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation (déclaration annuelle au Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March each calendar year, confirming that the beneficial ownership data on file is accurate and complete.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing incurs administrative fines up to EUR 5,000; false declarations incur criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and/or imprisonment; persistent default triggers a public negative flag and potential RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts publication (dépôt des comptes annuels) – required only if the SCSp exceeds small-entity exemption thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations – RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end (for a 31 December financial year-end, by 31 July); small partnerships under Article 27 of the Law of 19 December 2002 are exempt from filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If publication is required and omitted, fines range from EUR 1,000 to EUR 10,000; long-term default may lead to compulsory strike-off from the RCS after judicial notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income tax return (déclaration collective de revenus for the SCSp, tax transparent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the year following the financial year (calendar-year standard); extensions may be requested via the ACD electronic filing portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing yields monthly late interest of 0.6% on due tax, administration fines up to EUR 2,500, tax assessment at the ACD's discretion, and, for very serious and persistent failures, court-ordered strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is triggered when the SCSp exceeds any two of the three Luxembourg small-entity criteria under the Law of 19 December 2002: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50. A pure-equity-holding SCSp normally qualifies for exemption; mandatory audit also applies if the SCSp is registered as an alternative investment fund (AIFM Law) or is otherwise required by its partnership agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Normalisé) in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; voluntary IFRS adoption is permitted for the presentation of consolidated or individual accounts when not required by law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019, the SCSp must keep a current register of beneficial owners and electronically confirm the recorded particulars each year by 31 March. Any change in beneficial ownership, including those caused by transfer of partnership interests, must be filed with the RBE within one month of the change becoming known to the general partner.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (Registre des Associés Commanditaires)
Register of General Partner and Management (Registre des Gérants / Associés Commandités)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
Minute Book / Partnership Resolutions (Registre des Procès-Verbaux et Décisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 3,000 per annum (typical Luxembourg domiciliation/registered agent fee including AML/KYC compliance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 – statutory audit not required for a qualifying small SCSp; voluntary certified audit costs for a pure-holding SPV typically range from USD 8,000 to USD 20,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level (fiscally transparent special limited partnership; partners are assessable). For a comparable corporate tax payer in Luxembourg City, aggregate CIT rate is 24.94% (17% CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualified dividend income and capital gains from ≥10% or ≥€1.2 million holdings held ≥12 months, where the underlying subsidiary is subject to equal to or more than 15% CIT. IP Box regime: 80% exemption on qualifying intellectual property income. SCSp itself pays no corporate tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 537 (Déclaration de renseignements pour sociétés de personnes) — annual partnership information return; e-filed through the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration's eCDF portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 31 December when filed electronically; further extension available on application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp identification: Luxembourg RCS number, NACE code 6420, registered office, and name of the manager or general partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg registration number; no Luxembourg CIT withholding certificate is required for a transparent entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year and accounting date: indicate the opening and closing date of the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Normally calendar year; non-resident partners may use a special year-end only if supported by proper accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Global net accounting profit or loss of the SCSp before allocation; report all Luxembourg-source income and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State allocable shares for each partner; no tax is computed at the SCSp level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption schedule: list each subsidiary, holding percentage, acquisition cost, 12-month holding evidence, and the subsidiary's tax status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must show the subsidiary is subject to a minimum 15% corporate tax or is a Luxembourg taxable entity to obtain the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner schedule: name, country of tax residence, profit-sharing percentage, capital account, and contribution type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include each non-resident partner's tax residence and the relevant double tax treaty article allocating Luxembourg-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit schedule under Article 134bis for creditable foreign withholding or income taxes paid by the underlying subsidiary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are generally ineligible for Luxembourg unilateral credit if the treaty prescribes an exemption method; treaty relief may be claimed separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge on the assessed tax; unpaid tax accrues monthly interest of 0.6%; negligent or fraudulent understatement attracts additional fines from 20% to 50% of the tax due and may lead to criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for SCSp profit distributions because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and no dividend withholding tax applies at partnership level. Were the vehicle capitalized as a corporation, the statutory dividend WHT is 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying ≥10% holdings and under most Luxembourg tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a Luxembourg residence certificate via Form 24; attach the treaty partner's Tax Residency Certificate; claim reduced rates through the paying agent or file a refund claim with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration before 31 December of the following tax year; document legal ownership, beneficial ownership, and compliance with limitation-on-benefits clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg law: 0% withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest. Under Luxembourg's DTA network, royalties are treated at 0–5% and interest at 0–10% depending on the treaty, the beneficial owner, and the nature of the payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg's CbCR and Master File requirements apply to a multinational group with consolidated revenue of €750 million or above. A Local File is expected when a Luxembourg entity, including a pure holding SCSp, engages in controlled transactions exceeding €1 million annually, or financial transactions exceeding €100,000, consistent with Luxembourg TP administrative guidance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not impose quantitative Economic Substance Regulations, but EU-ATAD and OECD/BEPS principles require genuine commercial substance. A passive SCSp must maintain a physical Luxembourg office, resident managers, local board minutes, a Luxembourg bank account, and decision-making records. Failure to demonstrate such substance may result in denial of treaty benefits and participation exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting income, fabricating deductible expenses, misstating participation-exempt dividend income, or making false declarations on Form 537.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable base, default interest at 0.6% monthly, fines from 20% to 50% of under-declared tax; criminal fines for tax fraud typically range from €10,000 to €1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners are jointly and severally liable in civil restitution; courts may disregard legal personality and pierce the corporate veil upon fraud, imposing director disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 1 year in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a pure equity holding SCSp with no real economic activities, substance, or decision-making; appointing nominee directors; using the vehicle solely for treaty shopping or abusive intra-group financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp for Luxembourg tax purposes; denial of participation exemption and treaty benefits; recharacterization of outbound distributions as taxable income; administrative penalties up to 10% of the recomputed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the SCSp is an artificial construction; each director and manager is exposed to civil liability under Luxembourg company law (law of 10 August 1915), restitution orders, disqualification, and travel prohibitions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or maintain the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), concealing the ultimate beneficial owner behind the SCSp, or conducting undisclosed capital flows without proper KYC documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004, fines up to €1 million and penal sanctions; separate RBE non-disclosure fines up to €250,000 and publication of the violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal fines, freezing orders, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 2 years; regulators may also impose debarment from holding management functions in Luxembourg entities.
